data.title: Certificate Template Misconfiguration (AD CS)
data.summary: Certificate templates allowed low-privileged users to enrol for certificates permitting client authentication while supplying their own subject name. Any user could therefore obtain a certificate identifying them as any other user, including a domain administrator.
data.description:
Active Directory Certificate Services issues certificates according to templates, and a template that combines three properties becomes a domain-wide escalation: it permits enrolment by ordinary users, it grants an authentication purpose, and it lets the requester specify the subject alternative name.

A user enrols, names a domain administrator as the subject, and receives a valid certificate asserting that identity. Authentication with it is legitimate Kerberos — no password is involved, so password changes do not revoke it, and the certificate remains valid for its full lifetime.

Related misconfigurations include over-permissive enrolment rights on the CA itself and templates marked for manager approval that is not enforced. Templates accumulate over years and are rarely reviewed after deployment.
data.recommendation:
* Audit templates for enrollee-supplied subject names combined with authentication purposes, and remove one or the other.
* Require manager approval for templates that must remain flexible.
* Restrict enrolment rights to the groups that genuinely need each template.
* Treat the CA as a tier-0 asset with the same controls as a domain controller.
* Monitor certificate issuance, particularly requests naming privileged accounts.
data.short_recommendation: Remove requester-supplied subject names from enrollable templates.

attack_techniques.technique: T1649 — Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
